headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2003 S.B. 202). headings.title: Authorization required for pumping equipment connections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2003 S.B. 202). Clarifies that section 320.095 does not authorize connecting pumping equipment to water lines without authorization from the affected water supply's governing body.

headings.title: Prohibition on hard suction connections

headings.title: Monthly reporting of estimated emergency water use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2003 S.B. 202). Requires a fire protection service to notify any utilized water source of estimated emergency water usage on or before the 15th day of the following month for unaccounted-for water accountability.

headings.title: Minimum water-pressure depletion limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (L. 2003 S.B. 202). Prohibits any entity under any circumstance from depleting a water supply below the minimum pounds per square inch required by law or regulation.

headings.title: Personnel training on water systems, valves, and hydrants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (L. 2003 S.B. 202). Requires any entity contemplating emergency water use under section 320.095 to provide adequate personnel training on water system supply basics and proper valve and hydrant maintenance and operation.

headings.title: Fire-service liability for water system damages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (L. 2003 S.B. 202). Makes the fire protection entity liable for any damages it causes to any part of the water supply system from which water is taken.

headings.title: Permit requirement for fireworks manufacture, sale, and shipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1985 S.B. 76 § 2 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Makes manufacturing, selling, offering for sale, or shipping fireworks into or within Missouri unlawful without first obtaining the required state fire marshal permit and applicable federal permit/license, applying to residents and nonresidents alike.

headings.title: Permit issuance, minimum age, and calendar-year expiration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Authorizes and directs the state fire marshal to issue fireworks sale permits, bars issuance to persons under age 18, and sets December 31 expiration for all permits except seasonal retailers.

headings.title: Display of permits, nontransferability, and separate location permits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Requires displaying permits at the place of business, prohibits transferring or operating under another person's or location's permit, and requires separate permits for each location of multi-location manufacturers, wholesalers, annual retailers, and distributors.

headings.title: May 31 application deadline and discretionary refusal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Provides that failure to apply for a permit by May 31 may result in the fire marshal refusing to issue a permit for that calendar year.

headings.title: Discretionary permit refusal for false application statements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Provides that any false statement or declaration on a permit application may result in refusal to issue a permit for up to three years.

headings.title: Schedule of permit and operator license fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (including subdivisions (1)-(9)) and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Authorizes the state fire marshal to assess specified calendar-year permit fees (manufacturer, distributor, wholesaler, annual retailer, seasonal retailer, outdoor display, proximate-audience display) and three-year license fees (display operator and pyrotechnic effects operator).

headings.title: Sales authorized under manufacturer permit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Clarifies that manufacturer permit holders need no additional permits to sell to distributors, wholesalers, annual retailers, or seasonal retailers, or to sell "display, or articles pyrotechnic" (retaining archived omission of "fireworks" after "display", unlike subsection 8).

headings.title: Sales authorized under distributor permit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Clarifies that distributor permit holders need no additional permits to sell to wholesalers, annual retailers, or seasonal retailers, or to sell display fireworks or articles pyrotechnic.

headings.title: Seasonal retail sales authorized under annual retailer permit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Clarifies that annual retailer permit holders need no additional permit to sell consumer fireworks at retail during the fireworks season from their permanent structure.

headings.title: Fee deposit allocation and multiple-classification fee rule
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 (including subdivisions (1)(a)-(b) and (2)) and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Directs depositing 80% of collected fees into the section 320.094 fire education fund and 20% into the section 320.371 fund, and requires persons in multiple permit classifications to pay one permit fee based on the highest-revenue classification.

headings.title: Fire marshal enforcement, peace-officer assistance, and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Charges the state fire marshal with enforcing sections 320.106 to 320.161 with state, county, or city peace-officer assistance, authorizes chapter 536 rulemaking including operator training, testing, and licensing based on nationally recognized standards, and requires chapter 536 compliance for chapter rules to take effect.

headings.title: Discretionary permit withholding for unpaid state sales taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Authorizes the state fire marshal, upon department of revenue notice, to withhold permits upon evidence of unpaid prior-year state sales taxes, except when an applicant is pursuing a proper legal remedy challenging the tax.

headings.title: Permanent structure, code compliance, and fire-safety inspections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Requires distributors, wholesalers, and annual retailers to operate from code-compliant permanent structures, requires seasonal locations to comply with applicable building and fire regulations, and subjects applicants to potential state fire marshal inspections under promulgated rules.

headings.title: Verification of seasonal retailer permit before resale purchases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Prohibits manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, and annual retailers from selling consumer fireworks to a seasonal retailer lacking a current state fire marshal permit and requires seasonal retailers purchasing for in-state resale to acquire and present the permit beforehand.

headings.title: Premises inspections and seller cooperation during business hours
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 15 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Authorizes the state fire marshal and deputies to inspect premises and building portions where fireworks are stored, manufactured, kept, or offered for sale during normal business hours and requires full cooperation from sellers and offerors.

headings.title: Civil penalty for unpermitted fireworks operations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 16 and history note (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174). Imposes an additional civil penalty of up to $1,000 per day of operation (maximum $10,000) on any person manufacturing, selling, offering, or shipping fireworks into Missouri for use in Missouri without the required permit (retaining archived duplicate wording "ships or causes to be shipped into or caused to be shipped into").

headings.title: Testing, certification, and marking prerequisites and ASTM standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)-(8)) and source notes (L. 2009 H.B. 205; effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Prohibits Missouri cigarette sales (except under subsection 7) unless tested under ASTM E2187-04, certified under section 320.356, and marked under section 320.359, specifying ten-layer filter paper, 25% full-length burn cap across 40 replicates, ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation, 0.19 repeatability limit, no duplicate testing requirement, and fire marshal compliance testing.

headings.title: Lowered permeability band placement requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Requires certified cigarettes using lowered permeability bands to have at least two nominally identical bands positioned at specified minimum millimeter distances from the lighting end and filter or labeled end.

headings.title: Alternative test methods and multistate reciprocity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Requires manufacturers of cigarettes untestable under ASTM E2187-04 to propose equivalent alternative methods for state fire marshal approval, and directs accepting another comparable state's approved alternative unless the fire marshal demonstrates a reasonable basis to reject it.

headings.title: Manufacturer test-report retention and daily noncompliance penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Requires manufacturers to retain all cigarette test reports for three years and provide copies upon written request to the state fire marshal and attorney general, subject to a civil penalty up to $10,000 per day after 60 days of noncompliance.

headings.title: Adoption of subsequent ASTM ignition-strength standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Authorizes the state fire marshal to adopt a subsequent ASTM ignition-strength standard upon finding it does not change full-length burn percentages compared with ASTM E2187-04 and subsection 1(3).

headings.title: Triennial effectiveness review and report to general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Directs the state fire marshal to review section effectiveness and report findings and appropriate legislative recommendations to the general assembly every three years by June 30.

headings.title: Exceptions for pre-2011 stamped inventory and consumer testing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 (including subdivisions (1)-(2)) and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Exempts wholesaler or retailer sales of existing inventory stamped and purchased before January 1, 2011, and sales solely for manufacturer-controlled "consumer testing" as defined.

headings.title: Uniformity with other states' ignition propensity laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Directs implementing sections 320.350 to 320.374 to obtain uniformity with states having enacted reduced cigarette ignition propensity standards as of January 1, 2011.

headings.title: Required cigarette and laboratory details in certifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)-(10)) and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). headings.title: Agency access, public brand directory, and lawful-sale rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). headings.title: Three-year recertification requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Requires every cigarette certified under section 320.356 to be recertified every three years.

headings.title: Brand-family certification fee and coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Requires manufacturers to pay a $1,000 fee per certified brand family to the state fire marshal, covering all cigarettes and newly certified cigarettes in that family during the three-year period.

headings.title: Retesting requirement and sales ban for altered cigarettes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Prohibits selling a certified cigarette after any change likely to alter ignition-propensity compliance until retested with records maintained under section 320.353, and bars selling noncompliant altered cigarettes.

headings.title: Required FSC package compliance marking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2009 H.B. 205; effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Requires section 320.356 certified cigarettes to carry permanent eight-point or larger "FSC" markings at or near the UPC code indicating section 320.353 compliance.

headings.title: Single uniform marking across manufacturer packages and brands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Requires a manufacturer to use only one marking uniformly across all packs, cartons, cases, other packages, and brands it markets.

headings.title: Certification copies for wholesalers and marking inspections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Requires certifying manufacturers to provide copies of certifications to all wholesalers to which they sell, and requires wholesalers and retailers to allow department of revenue and attorney general inspection of package markings.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2009 H.B. 205; effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). headings.title: Civil penalties for retail knowing sales violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). headings.title: Civil penalties for knowingly false manufacturer certifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Imposes an additional civil penalty of $75,000 to $250,000 per knowingly false section 320.356 certification by a cigarette manufacturer.

headings.title: Civil penalties for other statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Imposes a civil penalty up to $1,000 for a first offense and up to $5,000 per subsequent violation of any other provision of sections 320.350 to 320.374.

headings.title: Fourteen-day sequestration of uncertified or unmarked cigarettes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Mandates 14-day owner sequestration without sale or transfer upon attorney general or department discovery of uncertified (§ 320.356) or unmarked (§ 320.359) cigarettes while the attorney general may petition for injunctive relief, permitting lawful sale if no action is filed within 14 days.

headings.title: Attorney general judicial remedies, separate violations, and judgment notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (including subdivisions (1)-(2) and the nested <div> continuation paragraph inside subdivision (2)) and source notes (effective 1-01-11; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Authorizes attorney general court actions for injunctive relief and recovery of state costs, damages, enforcement costs, and attorney's fees, makes each statutory or rule violation a separate civil violation, and requires sending injunctive judgments to affected wholesalers.

headings.title: Fund creation, revenue sources, administration, and fire-safety use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2009 H.B. 205, A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). headings.title: Exemption from biennial reversion to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Exempts unexpended fund balances at biennium end from reverting to general revenue under section 33.080.

headings.title: Fund investment and crediting of earnings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (A.L. 2025 S.B. 81 & 174; contingent termination date, see section 320.374). Directs the state treasurer to invest fund moneys like other funds and credit investment interest and earnings to the fund.

headings.title: Exception for cigarettes stamped or packaged for outside sales
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2009 H.B. 205; effective 1-01-11). headings.title: Contingent termination upon federal ignition propensity standard

headings.title: Board of trustees authority to modify program and limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)-(3)) and source notes (A.L. 2023 S.B. 24 merged with S.B. 186). headings.title: Pool board as public governmental body under chapter 610
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (A.L. 2023 S.B. 24 merged with S.B. 186). Designates the pool board of trustees as a public governmental body subject to all provisions of chapter 610.

headings.title: Pool authority to accept public or private grants and donations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (A.L. 2023 S.B. 24 merged with S.B. 186). Authorizes a pool to accept or apply for grants or donations from any private or public source.

headings.title: State fire marshal pool grants and 287.245 funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (including subdivisions (1)-(2)) and source notes (A.L. 2023 S.B. 24 merged with S.B. 186). headings.title: Workers' compensation determinations, offsets, and employer subrogation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 (including subdivisions (1)-(3)) and source notes (A.L. 2023 S.B. 24 merged with S.B. 186). headings.title: Definitions and chapter 198 facility exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)-(3)) and source notes (L. 2026 S.B. 1421; severability clause, see section 1.1010). Defines "Division", "Missouri fire and life safety standards" (informed by IFC, IBC, and NFPA without adopting any model code in whole), and "State-inspected facility" (excluding chapter 198 licensed facilities).

headings.title: Adoption by July 2027, incorporation limits, and five-year review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)-(4)) and source notes (L. 2026 S.B. 1421; severability clause, see section 1.1010). Requires adopting Missouri fire and life safety standards by rule no later than July 1, 2027, permits selective technical incorporation while prohibiting adopting any model code in whole, allows Missouri-specific modifications, and requires reviewing standards at least every five years with chapter 536 updates.

headings.title: Triggering events for applicability beginning January 1, 2028
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)-(4)) and source notes (L. 2026 S.B. 1421; severability clause, see section 1.1010). Applies Missouri fire and life safety standards beginning January 1, 2028 to state-inspected facilities upon initial construction, major renovation affecting egress/detection/alarm/suppression, ownership transfer, or aggregate substantial improvement (>=50% preimprovement market value without requiring a formal appraisal).

headings.title: Qualified nonconforming status of pre-August 28, 2026 facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (L. 2026 S.B. 1421; severability clause, see section 1.1010). Treats state-inspected facilities existing before August 28, 2026 as lawfully nonconforming and exempt from complying with the standards except as triggered under subsection 3.

headings.title: Local stringency rules and scope disclaimer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (including subdivisions (1)-(3)) and source notes (L. 2026 S.B. 1421; severability clause, see section 1.1010). Permits cities, counties, and fire protection districts to adopt stricter standards, prohibits political subdivisions from applying less stringent standards to regulated facilities, and disclaims creating a statewide building or fire code for occupancies not already division-inspected.

headings.title: Compliance inspections, licensing prerequisite, and enforcement remedies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (including subdivisions (1)-(3)) and source notes (L. 2026 S.B. 1421; severability clause, see section 1.1010). Requires compliance verification via division or authorized local inspections, bars licensing, certifying, or approving a state-inspected facility without division compliance determination, and authorizes correction orders, reinspections, or occupancy limitations.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance under chapter 536 and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes (L. 2026 S.B. 1421; section-level note cites severability clause in section 1.1010).
